newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL overnight up at 7.2/5 pct as interbank falls.
newsitem.headline: KL overnight up at 7.2/5 pct as interbank falls.

text.p: The overnight interbank rate was slightly higher at 7.2/5 percent at 0800 GMT against a closing of 6.5 percent on Friday after other interbank rates fell sharply in early trading, dealers said on Monday.
Dealers said the maturity of a 500 million ringgit Bank Negara Bill issue on Friday and expectation of further increase in liquidity this week pulled down other interbank rates.
"It is not clear why the overnight has gone up today. Maybe there is some temporary mismatch in funds flow, but it should come down in line with other rates," a dealer with a Malaysian bank said.
On Wednesday, 420 million ringgit will mature from a long-term government bond and, on Friday, 500 million ringgit in Bank Negara bills.
"The central bank has no plans to roll over the funds at the moment, which means the market's tightness will ease further," one dealer said.
One-week interbank rate fell to 6.90/7.10 percent against 7.8/8.0 on Friday, two-week to 7.00/30 percent against 7.50/70 and three-week to 7.10/25 percent from 7.40/50.
One-month money eased to 7.20/30 percent from 7.40/45, three-month to 7.25/30 percent from 7.40/45 and six-month to 7.30/35 percent from 7.45/50, the dealers said.
Interest rate futures on the Malaysia Monetary Exchange were mixed, as investors cut their losses after the sudden reversal in the spot rate trend, futures dealers said.
The benchmark three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (KLIBOR) June contract was steady at 92.67, or an implied yield of 7.33 percent.
But, September was steady at 92.65, or 7.35 percent, and December unchanged at 92.63, or 7.37 percent. They were up sharply before lunch.
